messages:
Diego - Sales: New POC kickoff with GlobalBank. Requirement: customer data must never egress to US for inference, logs, telemetry. They asked for EU + Canada only. Need quick answers for SOW + risk table.
Ravi - Infra Eng: Quick take: We can pin inference workloads to europe-west1 and northamerica-northeast1. However control-plane (accounting/meta orchestration) lives in us-central by default. That means usages/metrics/trace IDs could touch US endpoints unless we do Private or Dedicated with control-plane residency.
Sophie - Solutions Eng: Clarify what "never egress" means for them: payloads, model weights, KV cache, logs, monitoring? There are different levers. We can keep payloads and model execution region-local but endpoints for telemetry and rollout signaling might not.
Diego - Sales: They explicitly called out payloads, logs, and audit trails. Also asked about sticky-session behavior (session affinity) — they don't want sessions to failover out of region.
Marta - Security: If logs + audit trails cannot leave region, Hosted isn't sufficient. We can redact logs before sending out, but full audit trails for operations will still traverse control-plane. BYO-KMS where keys never leave region is possible but requires Private or a dedicated control-plane instance that respects KMS locality.
Claire - Legal: We need to know subprocessor list scoped to EU/CA for contract addendum. Also confirm whether we can sign an amendment that limits subprocessors for this customer during the POC.
Ravi - Infra Eng: Subprocessor sketch: GCP eu-west (data plane), GCP ca-north, monitoring partner (EU deployment available), log-aggregation partner (primarily US but can be configured to EU-only for some customers). I can request an attestation PDF for subprocessors scoped to this POC.
Sophie - Solutions Eng: Routing policy options we can offer:
1) STRICT_PIN: requests and KV cache pinned to allowed regions, failover disabled
2) AFFINITY_ONLY: try allowed regions first, fallback allowed but prefixed with audit tag
3) BEST_EFFORT: prioritize region but fallback normally
Example config:
```
routing:
  policy: STRICT_PIN
  allowed_regions: [europe-west1, northamerica-northeast1]
  session_affinity: true
  allow_fallback: false
```
Diego - Sales: Can we get a one-liner for Legal that states limitations clearly?
Claire - Legal: One-liner: "Redwood can pin inference and customer payloads to EU + Canada regions for the POC; however, control-plane metadata (accounting, rollout signals, and aggregated telemetry) will continue to be processed in our control plane hosted in the US unless a Private deployment is procured. Exceptions (e.g., full control-plane residency) require a separate enterprise agreement and onboarding timeline."
Marta - Security: Additional notes: retention of debug logs can be set to 0 for hosted; we can also enable redaction to strip PII before export. If customer requires verifiable in-region keys, BYO-KMS with HSM and an in-region key policy pushes us to Private.
E2E-Bot: Ticket created: POC-5872 — geo-pin + subproc attestation request. Owners: Ravi, Sophie. ETA: 4 business days for attachments.
Ravi - Infra Eng: For SOW pricing impact: geo-pin w/ strict pinning => extra egress isolation overhead and smaller multi-tenant pooling efficiency. Ballpark: +20-45% per unit depending on concurrency and model. Dedicated reserved pools will reduce delta. I'll provide a short cost table in the ticket.
Sophie - Solutions Eng: Also flag: disabling failover affects availability. Recommend SLA caveat in SOW: "Geo-pin with failover disabled may impact availability; SLA exceptions possible."
Diego - Sales: Thanks. Claire, can you confirm whether the one-liner is sufficient for DD? If not, we'll ask for wording tweaks.
Claire - Legal: Works for initial DD. I'll ask procurement to review the subproc attestation and will loop in Privacy for the log retention/redaction language.
Diego - Sales: Next steps: 1) Ravi to attach scoped subprocessor PDF to POC-5872; 2) Sophie to add routing config + cost table; 3) Marta to confirm redaction/KMS notes; 4) Legal to review and sign off on caveat language. We'll reconvene in #POC-5872 thread.
